A very warm welcome from our Executive Headteacher
A Welcome from the Executive Headteacher
It is my pleasure to welcome you to St Paul’s and All Hallows’ Infant and Junior Schools. Our school community is committed to providing an exceptional education for every child, where high standards, strong values and a culture of continuous improvement sit at the heart of all that we do.
Our vision, learning to love and loving to learn, underpins every aspect of school life. We aim to cultivate curiosity, empathy and a genuine enjoyment of learning, inspiring children to develop both academically and personally. We believe that education should enable pupils to thrive as confident, responsible and compassionate individuals who are well prepared for the opportunities and challenges ahead.
Our approach is built on the understanding that small, deliberate steps lead to significant and lasting achievement. Careful attention to detail, consistent reflection and a commitment to improvement ensure that each child’s progress is continually supported. This philosophy allows us to nurture ambition, promote excellence and ensure that every pupil benefits from a rich and thoughtfully planned educational experience.
St Paul’s and All Hallows’ is a diverse and welcoming community where every child is known and valued. The personalised attention possible within our small school setting enables us to support each pupil’s individual strengths and needs. Our dedicated staff work closely with families to ensure that every child feels safe, cared for and motivated to achieve their very best.
Our core values of friendship, wisdom, forgiveness, compassion, perseverance and courage shape our ethos and guide our expectations. These values inform our curriculum, which is designed to foster deep knowledge, creativity, resilience and cultural understanding. We are committed to the principles of scholarship and provide every pupil, regardless of background, with the ambition and practical tools needed to succeed both in school and in life.
We strive to create an environment in which pupils are happy, inspired and eager to attend each day. Through high quality teaching, an ambitious curriculum and a persistent focus on what truly matters for great learning, we aim to prepare our pupils for a future filled with choice, opportunity and the confidence to contribute meaningfully to society.
Thank you for taking the time to learn more about St Paul’s and All Hallows’ Schools. We warmly invite you to visit us and experience our community in person.
Christalla Jamil Executive Headteacher
The LDBS Academies Trust

Our mission is to establish, maintain, carry on, manage and develop Church of England Schools across the Diocese of London. Our aim is that every child should have the opportunity to flourish and develop into a rounded adult who can live life to the full.

School Vision and Values
Our School Verse
Let all that you do be done in love.
(1 Corinthians 16 v 13)
‘Let all you do, be done in love,’ is a well-known verse by the Apostle Paul, our Patron Saint.
It emphasises the importance of love as part of the Christian ethos.
The verse encourages us at SPAH to approach all our actions, interactions, and decisions towards the whole school community, with a spirit of love.
Our School Vision
We are a Christian community, united in love, where every individual grows in wisdom, builds deep friendships and practises true forgiveness. We Challenge ourselves in all that we do so that we each can flourish and become the person God is calling us to be.
Our School Values
Compassion Courage Friendship Perseverance Wisdom Forgiveness
Our School History
The crossed swords are the symbol for St Paul and the Christ the King symbol is presumably for All Hallows’. The church was until the 15th century called All Saints. Interestingly All Hallows is in the gift of St Paul’s cathedral so the crossed swords are doubly important as that is their symbol too.
All Hallows’ celebration day is November 1st.
St Paul’s day is January 25th and is the celebration of his conversion.
The last Sunday before Advent is ‘Christ the King’ Sunday. The Gospel set for that day is about Jesus the Good Shepherd also being the King and the judge. He wades into the sheep and goats and separates them, the sheep that have helped the poor and needy are rewarded and the goats who have been greedy and uncaring of others are condemned.
The last Sunday before Advent is also known as ‘Stir up’ Sunday which is what the shepherd did with the sheep and the goats. Traditionally, the day was the day everyone then went home from church and made their Christmas puddings or cakes, and everyone in the family had a stir.

Welcome
A welcome from our Executive Headteacher:
Welcome to St Paul’s and All Hallows’ CE Infant and Junior School. We provide high-quality education for all of our children, which is based on nurturing excellence. We challenge ourselves in all we do, so as to flourish and become the people God is calling us to be.
We are a Christian community directed by the Biblical verse:
Let all that you do be done in love. (1 Corinthians 16 v 13)
We encourage open communication and strive to develop our children into responsible and successful global citizens.
Our core values are friendship, wisdom and forgiveness, compassion, perseverance and courage that underpin all we do and help shape our ambitious curriculum, through which the children enjoy learning and are equipped for a successful future.
Our curriculum is designed to develop all children’s academic and creative abilities, mental and physical wellbeing through our Christian vision in engaging all members of our community (pupils & staff alike) offering them new and exciting learning opportunities.
​Children who attend our school are of diverse backgrounds. Their unique and personal development to their full potential is enabled by the individual and personalised attention provided at this small school.
St Paul’s and All Hallows’ Schools are blessed with a supportive community consisting of staff, a strong leadership team, uniquely individual children and supportive parents. We want everyone within our community to flourish and achieve a life-long love of learning.
We strongly believe achievement and enjoyment go hand in hand and we have high expectations in all areas. There is a strong focus on the development of the children’s spiritual, moral, social and cultural understanding so that they know how to make positive contributions to their community and wider society.
We invite you to come and see for yourself all that St Paul’s and All Hallows’ Schools have to offer. I look forward to meeting you in person.
Executive Headteacher

Being A Church School
The Church of England has a long and respected history of involvement of education.
Church of England schools are established primarily for the communities they are located in and were founded by parishes to serve the poorest children. They are inclusive and serve equally those who are of the Christian faith, those of other faiths and those with no faith.
You can read more about Church of England schools here.

pageCache.text:
Remote Learning
We are committed to delivering high quality education, including for remote learning, whether for homework or during periods of remote working and learning. We recognise the importance of maintaining high expectations in all areas of school life, including remote learning.
In line with DfE guidance we have reviewed our Remote Learning here.
Please refer to our Remote Learning Strategy to find out more and for information about safeguarding and staying safe online. The plan includes copies of Acceptable Use Agreements that all pupils agree to – we ask that parents/carers also review the agreements with their children to remind them of the expectations.
Google Classroom is the remote learning platform used by the school. The work that your child is given is suited to their age, interests and ability. If you are having trouble logging in, email admin@spah.haringey.sch.uk
Please see this guide on how to use a games console to access learning.
In addition to the work set on Google Classroom, children must read to an adult at home every night during the week and at least once over the weekend. The adult, who listens to a child read, should then sign their reading diary to acknowledge that they have heard them read.
The school also subscribes to the resources below for use both in and out of school.
If you can’t remember your password, please ask your class teacher or email office@spahschool.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: St Paul's and All Hallows' Infant and Junior Schools - The School Day
pageCache.text:
The School Day
Our schools are organised in such a way as to provide maximum time for learning across a balanced curriculum.
Our schools are committed to offering our children a healthy start to the school day by inviting them to attend a Breakfast Club from 8.00am each day. Places in our Breakfast Club can be arranged through the main school office, and cost £1.50 a day.
Both schools begin 8.45am and finish at 3.15pm.
In our schools, the mornings are usually given to Phonics, Reading, Writing and Maths. Depending on the year group, the order in which these are taught may vary.
All of our EYFS, KS1 and KS2 children have a fifteen minute break in the middle of the morning.
Play time and lunchtime staff are trained to support children’s play. There are a wide range of activities for children to enjoy, such as skipping, reading, drawing and sports. Infant lunch starts from 11:45am and Junior lunch starts at 12:15pm
Our afternoons are filled with learning based on the wider curriculum. Subjects taught include Science, Geography, History and Art. In addition to these, the children are also taught Design Technology, French, Computing, Physical Education and Music.
